title: Ph.D. Project AIM: Accelerating Arbitrary-Precision Integer Multiplication on Heterogeneous Reconfigurable Computing Platform Versal ACAP
problem: Arbitrary-precision integer multiplication requires decomposing large integers and performing parallel byte-level low-bit multiplications, followed by shifting and adding results through long bit-level propagation chains. Current hardware accelerators are not optimally designed for both computation phases simultaneously.
motivation: Arbitrary-precision multiplication is essential for cryptographic algorithms and scientific computing, but existing FPGA implementations show lower energy efficiency than CPU and GPU alternatives.
method: AIM leverages the heterogeneous AMD Versal ACAP platform containing 400 AI Engine (AIE) processors, an FPGA, and an ARM CPU. The framework assigns the parallel byte-level multiplication phase to 400 AIEs which have efficient vector units, and assigns the sequential bit-level addition/shifting phase to the FPGA which has optimized DSPs and LUTs.
key_novelty: Strategic partitioning of arbitrary-precision multiplication computation across heterogeneous resources optimized for different algorithmic patterns: AIEs for parallel byte-level operations and FPGA for sequential bit-level processing.
contributions: Identifies that dedicated vector units optimize the parallel multiplication phase while DSPs/LUTs better suit the sequential addition phase
Proposes AIM framework orchestrating computation across heterogeneous resources on Versal ACAP
Achieves 12.6x energy efficiency gain over Intel Xeon CPU and 2.1x over Nvidia A5000 GPU
Open-sources implementation with validation on cryptographic (RSA), arithmetic, and visualization (Mandelbrot) workloads
limitations: Generalization to other heterogeneous platforms and comparison with other ACAP configurations not discussed.
primary_theme: Heterogeneous resource scheduling for arbitrary-precision arithmetic
